facts.fact: The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10 of 31 March 2025 orders payment service providers to move low-value cross-border transfers within the Common Monetary Area from the SADC-RTGS arrangement to the TCIB scheme by 1 April 2027.

NAM.note: Directive speaks of cost-effectiveness for users but sets no consumer-protection rule.

facts.fact: The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10 says cross-border low-value electronic transfers within the Common Monetary Area are currently settled through a temporary SADC-RTGS arrangement, to cease by 31 March 2027 in favour of TCIB.

The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10 requires payment service providers to execute low-value Common Monetary Area transfers through the regional TCIB scheme from 1 April 2027, after the SADC-RTGS stopgap ends on 31 March 2027.

NAM.note: Nothing on government payments to people.

facts.fact: The Bank of Namibia issued Directive PSDIR-10 under section 44 of the Payment System Management Act, 2023 (Act No. 14 of 2023), effective on signature on 31 March 2025, with contravention an offence.
Directive PSDIR-10 sets the regulator's deadline of 1 April 2027 for payment service providers to execute low-value cross-border Common Monetary Area transfers through the TCIB scheme.

NAM.note: No survey share of adults with accounts.
A CMA oversight committee position paper is not a treaty, act or agreement of the kinds asked.

facts.fact: The Bank of Namibia's Directive PSDIR-10, in line with the Common Monetary Area Cross-border Payments Oversight Committee position paper of 31 July 2024, made the move of low-value CMA transfers to TCIB binding at home.

NAM.note: Nothing on retail mobile money or a national switch.
Nothing on tax or fee payment.
